THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S.439 CR.P.C PRAYING TO ENLARGE AND GRANT BAIL TO THE PETITIONER IN CR.NO.125/2024 REGISTERED BY THE 1ST RESPONDENT SUBRAMANYANAGAR POLICE MALLESHWARAM SUB DIVISION FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 3(1)(R),
3(1)(S) U/S. SC/ST (POA) 1989 THE OFFENCE P/U/S 4, 6, 8, 12 OF PCOSO ACT AND SEC.3, 4 OF DP ACT AND FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 354(C), 376, 498, 506, 34 OF IPC WHICH IS PENDING BEFORE THE ADDITIONAL CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE FTSC II BENGALURU.

THIS CRL.P, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner-accused No.1 is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in Crime No. 125/2024 of Subramanyanagar Police Station, Malleswaram Sub-Division, pending on the file of the learned Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge-FTSC-II, Bengaluru, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s) of SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989 (in short "POA Act"), under Sections 4, 6, 8, 12 Of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
2012 (in short "POCSO Act"), and Sections 3, 4 Of Dowry Prohibition Act, and offence under Sections 354(c), 376, 498, 506, 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on NC:
2024:KHC:27153 the basis of the first information lodged by the informant - Radhika N.S.
2.

sentences.text: Heard Sri. K.N. Phanindra, Senior Advocate for Smt. Vaishali Hegde, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri. Rahul Rai K, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 -State and Sri. Kamaluddin Ahmad, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioner being accused No.1 is seeking grant of bail.
He was apprehended on 07.06.2024 and since then, he is in judicial custody.

sentences.text: The victim said to be aged 21 years (on 03.06.2024) filed the first information making serious allegations against the petitioner for having committed the offences as stated above.

But admittedly,
respondent No.2 as informant had filed the complaint registered in NCR No.50/2024 and the petitioner and the co-accused were granted anticipatory bail by this Court in Crl.P.No.3892/2024 vide order dated 27.05.2024.
Immediately, thereafter, on 03.06.2024, the present information came to be filed making serious allegations about the offence committed by the petitioner, during 2019.
Admittedly, respondent No.2 after attaining majority had married the petitioner and it is stated that their marriage was registered on 13.01.2023.
However, the informant states that the marriage and the registration of the marriage was against her wishes.
The same is to be proved by the prosecution during trial.
I do not find any reason to detain the petitioner in the custody.
It is stated that accused Nos.2 and 3 are already enlarged on bail and accused No.4 who is a distant relative of the petitioner is granted anticipatory bail.

Considering all these facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petitioner NC: 2024:KHC:27153 is entitled to be enlarged on bail subject to conditions, which will take care of the interest of the prosecution.
6. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime 125/2024 of Subramanyanagar Police Station, Malleswaram Sub-Division, on obtaining the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court, subject to the following conditions:
a). The petitioner shall not commit similar offences.
b). The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c).
The petitioner shall appear before the Court as and when required.
If in case, the petitioner violates any of the conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to move the Trial Court seeking cancellation of bail.

On furnishing the sureties by the petitioner, the Trial Court is at liberty to direct the Investigating Officer to verify NC: 2024:KHC:27153 the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by the petitioner and the sureties and a report may be called for in that regard,
which is to be submitted by the Investigating Officer within 5 days.

The Trial Court on satisfaction,
may proceed to accept the sureties for the purpose of releasing the petitioner on bail.
